metadata.description: Mem0 Initial Facts for 3 User Personas – seed data for long-term memory system

personas.first_timer: Nguyen Van Minh – Marketing professional, B1 English, goal: professional communication
personas.speed_runner: Tran Thi Lan – IT Engineer, B2 English, goal: IELTS 7.0 in 3 months
personas.qa_destroyer: Le Quoc Bao – Finance analyst, C1 English, goal: C-suite presentation English

alpha_quality_review.method: PII-safe existing fact review + duplicate-key decontamination marker

profile.name: Nguyen Van Minh
profile.primary_goal: Write professional emails and give presentations in English

facts.content: Minh consistently uses 'discuss about' instead of 'discuss'. This L1 interference error has appeared in 4 out of 5 writing sessions.
facts.evidence: Appeared in email writing exercises on Jan 8, 9, 10. Corrected twice but reverted.

facts.content: Minh frequently omits articles before singular countable nouns, especially in formal writing contexts (e.g., 'I have meeting tomorrow').
facts.evidence: 15 article omission errors documented across 3 writing exercises.

facts.content: Minh uses present simple instead of present perfect with 'already', 'yet', and 'just' (e.g., 'I already sent the report' instead of 'I have already sent the report').
facts.evidence: Error pattern seen in 3 email drafts when reporting task completion to manager.

facts.content: Minh learns best through real-world marketing scenarios. Responds positively to examples using familiar brands (Vinamilk, Unilever Vietnam). Abstract grammar rules without context cause disengagement.
facts.evidence: Completion rate 85% for scenario-based tasks vs 40% for pure grammar drills.

facts.content: Minh's energy level is highest on Monday and Tuesday mornings (energy level 4-5/5). Friday evenings show energy level 1-2/5 with higher error rates. Recommend scheduling challenging grammar topics early in the week.
facts.evidence: Tracked over 4-week period. Friday error rate 2.3x higher than Monday.

facts.content: Minh has mastered the 'make vs do' collocation distinction after 3 weeks of targeted practice. Error rate dropped from 80% to 8%. This pattern should no longer be prioritized in error correction.
facts.evidence: Assessment test on Jan 31: 92% accuracy on make/do collocations (up from 20% on Jan 10).

facts.content: Minh's immediate goal: write a professional campaign brief in English by end of February 2025. Long-term goal: present quarterly marketing report to regional management in English by Q3 2025.
facts.evidence: Stated in onboarding session and confirmed in Week 2 check-in.

facts.content: Minh frequently writes emails to: (1) international agency partners (formal register needed), (2) internal team (semi-formal), (3) senior management (formal, concise). Most pain point: starting emails professionally without sounding robotic.
facts.evidence: Interview during onboarding. Sample emails analyzed.

facts.content: Lan's IELTS Writing Task 2 essays consistently lack cohesion devices. Uses basic connectors (and, but, so) but rarely uses discourse markers (furthermore, nevertheless, in contrast, consequently).
facts.evidence: 3 practice essays scored Band 6.0 for Coherence & Cohesion. Examiner notes: 'limited range of cohesive devices'.

facts.content: Lan tends to overuse 'I think' and 'In my opinion' at the expense of more academic phrases. Does not vary opinion language: 'It could be argued that', 'It is widely believed that', 'Evidence suggests that'.
facts.evidence: Average 4 instances of 'I think' per essay. Lexical Resource score consistently 6.0.

facts.content: Lan struggles with IELTS Speaking Part 3 (abstract discussion topics). Gives short answers (1-2 sentences) instead of developing ideas with examples, reasons, and speculation (3-5 sentences minimum for Band 7).
facts.evidence: Mock test Part 3 average answer length: 28 words. Target for Band 7: 50-70 words.

facts.content: Lan is highly data-driven. Responds best to clear metrics (current score vs target score, % improvement). Gamification elements (streaks, accuracy %) significantly boost her engagement. Dislikes vague encouragement without data.
facts.evidence: Completion rate 95% for tasks with clear scoring rubrics vs 55% for open-ended tasks.

facts.content: Lan's IELTS Reading score has improved from 6.5 to 7.0 after 6 weeks of skimming/scanning practice. Reading is now her strongest skill. Redirect focus to Writing and Speaking for overall Band 7.
facts.evidence: Practice test Feb 15: Reading 7.0. Writing 6.0, Speaking 6.5, Listening 6.5.

facts.content: Lan is most productive between 6-8am (energy level 5/5). She enters a 'flow state' on problems that feel like engineering challenges (structured, logical). Abstract grammar discussions reduce her motivation.
facts.evidence: Self-reported in onboarding. Validated by 30% faster task completion in morning sessions.

facts.content: Deadline: IELTS exam booked for April 15, 2025. Target: Overall Band 7.0 (minimum Band 6.5 in each skill). Use case: Application to a senior engineering position at a Singapore tech company.
facts.evidence: Confirmed in onboarding and weekly check-ins. Exam registration confirmed.

profile.name: Le Quoc Bao
profile.primary_goal: Master C-suite level presentations and executive business communication

facts.content: Bao's spoken English is grammatically accurate but lacks executive presence. Uses hedging language excessively ('I think maybe', 'kind of', 'sort of') which undermines authority in C-suite settings.
facts.evidence: Presentation recording analysis: 12 instances of excessive hedging in 5-minute pitch. Executive coach feedback.

facts.content: Bao struggles with financial storytelling – presenting data with narrative structure. Tends to list numbers without connecting them to business implications or recommendations.
facts.evidence: Q4 board presentation feedback: 'Numbers presented but strategic implications unclear to non-finance audience'.

facts.content: Bao uses Vietnamese sentence rhythm in long English sentences, creating run-on structures. Example: 'The revenue increased significantly and we also saw improvement in EBITDA margin while the cash flow remained positive and this demonstrates our strategy is working.'
facts.evidence: Observed in 3 written reports and 2 verbal presentations.

facts.content: Bao is highly autonomous and dislikes being 'taught' basic concepts. Prefers: (1) being challenged to self-correct, (2) comparative analysis of his own output vs expert examples, (3) discussion-based learning over drills.
facts.evidence: Stated explicitly in onboarding. Disengaged when presented with A1-B1 level content by mistake.

facts.content: Bao has successfully integrated executive vocabulary (leverage, synergy, stakeholder alignment, runway, burn rate) into his speaking without sounding unnatural. Vocabulary range is now a strength. Focus should shift to delivery and narrative structure.
facts.evidence: Role-play assessment Feb 1: Vocabulary scoring excellent (C2 level terms used accurately in context).

facts.content: Bao is in high-stress periods during quarter-end (March, June, Sep, Dec). During these periods, reduce session depth and focus on quick, practical phrase refinements rather than deep analysis. Standard pace resumes post-close.
facts.evidence: Self-reported in onboarding. Confirmed by drop in session attendance in Dec (quarter-end).

facts.content: Bao's goal: Deliver a compelling 10-minute investor presentation in English at the regional CFO conference in June 2025. Secondary goal: Transition from 'competent non-native speaker' to 'indistinguishable from a native finance professional'.
facts.evidence: Primary goal stated in onboarding. Conference date confirmed: June 18, 2025.

facts.content: Bao regularly interacts with: (1) International investors (formal, data-heavy), (2) Singapore regional HQ (formal emails/calls), (3) Vietnamese direct reports (code-switching context). Most challenging: spontaneous Q&A after presentations.
facts.evidence: Stakeholder mapping exercise during onboarding. Confirmed by sample communications reviewed.
